items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to requiring annual radon testing of schools
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5753

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation
to requiring annual radon testing of schools

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to require annual radon testing of
facilities that care for residents with developmental disabilities.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Section 16.11 of the mental hygiene law is amended by
adding subdivision (g) which shall require annual radon testing in all
schools as defined in section 1.03 of mental hygiene law ("School"
means the in-patient service of a developmental center or other
residential facility for individuals with developmental disabilities
under the jurisdiction of the office for people with developmental
disabilities or a facility for the residential care, treatment,
training, or education of individuals with developmental disabilities
which has been issued an operating certificate by the commissioner of
developmental disabilities.) Such testing shall be performed by a
trained and certified, independent entity. Where radon levels exceed 4
pCi/L, corrective action shall be taken within the 30 days. Where
radon levels exceed 8 pCi/L, corrective action shall be taken within
14 days. Test results must be posted online. A comprehensive report of
test results shall be available each year by January 15th.

Section 2: All schools shall have their first annual radon test within
120 days of this act.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Under current law there is no requirement for radon gas testing at
facilities caring for the developmentally disabled. It is also
estimated that indoor radon gas exposure causes more than 21,000 lung
cancer deaths per year, making it the second leading lung cancer
threat after cigarettes. Conducting annual radon testing of these
facilities will help prevent lung cancer deaths for this already
vulnerable population and will ensure that corrective action is taken
to stop radon gas exposure.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S.8039A - Referred to Rules / A.10236A - Referred to Mental
Health.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to requiring annual radon testing of facilities, department facilities, hospitals, schools, community residences, supervised living facilities, supportive living facilities and residential care centers for adults
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5753B

SPONSOR: LANZA
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to
requiring annual radon testing of facilities, department facilities,
hospitals, schools, community residences, supervised living facilities,
supportive living facilities and residential care centers for adults

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to require annual radon testing of facili-
ties, department facilities, hospitals, schools, community residences,
supervised living facilities and other facilities

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Section 16.11 of the mental hygiene law is amended by adding
subdivision (g) which shall require annual radon testing of each facil-
ty, department facility, hospital, school, community residence, super-
vised living facility, supportive living facility and residential care
center for adults. Such testing shall be performed by a trained and
certified, independent entity. Where radon levels exceed 4 pCi/L,
corrective action shall be taken within the 30 days.  Where radon levels
exceed 8 pCi/L, corrective action shall be taken within 14 days. Test
results must be posted online. A comprehensive report of test results
shall be available each year by January 15th.

Section 2: The mental hygiene law is amended by adding a new section
31.39 to require annual radon testing of each facility, department
facility, hospital, school, community residence, supervised living
facility, supportive living facility and residential care center for
adults. Such testing shall be performed by a trained and certified,
independent entity. Where radon levels exceed 4 pCi/L, corrective action
shall be taken within the 30 days. Where radon levels exceed 8 pCi/L,
corrective action shall be taken within 14 days. Test results must be
posted online. A comprehensive report of test results shall be available
each year by January 15th.

Section 3: All facilities shall have their first annual radon test with-
in 120 days of this act.

Section 4: This act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law there is no requirement for radon gas testing at
facilities caring for the developmentally disabled. It is also estimated
that indoor radon gas exposure causes more than 21,000 lung cancer
deaths per year, making it the second leading lung cancer threat after
cigarettes. Conducting annual radon testing of these facilities will
help prevent lung cancer deaths for this already vulnerable population
and will ensure that corrective action is taken to stop radon gas expo-
sure.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017: S.5753-B - Passed Senate / A.5515-B - Referred to Mental Health
2016: S.8039A - Referred to Rules / A.10236A - Referred to Mental Health

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Minimal.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
